prompt: Why is searching for `aaaab` inside a long run of `a`s a bad case for naive left-to-right matching?

options.text: The first character mismatches immediately at every start.
options.explanation: The first four characters match, so each attempt does substantial repeated work.

options.text: The matcher skips five characters after every failure.
options.explanation: Naive matching moves to the next start and compares again.

options.text: Each attempt repeats the same successful prefix comparisons before failing near the end.
options.explanation: Correct. Earlier matching work is discarded at each new start.

options.text: The algorithm must build a suffix array before comparing.
options.explanation: Naive matching has no preprocessing index.

workedExample: Each attempt recognises the run of a characters, then fails on b. Moving one start to the right repeats almost the same comparisons. KMP retains useful matched-prefix information after the mismatch instead of restarting the text work.
